evidence.snippet: [단독] "러트닉이 막았다"… 트럼프, 엔비디아 칩 중국 유출 단속 3번 승인했지만 상무부 지연 [공부의여신 네트워크] 트럼프 대통령이 올해에만 세 차례 엔비디아 첨단 AI 칩을 중국으로 빼돌린 것으로 의심되는 기업들에 대한 단속을 승인했지만, 하워드 러트닉 상무장관이 번번이 이를 가로막아 왔다고 악시오스가 11일(현지시간) 고위 소식통 6명을 인용해 단독 보도했습니다. 보도에 따르면 스파이 스캔들로 행정부가 뒤숭숭하던 지난 5일(목), 러트닉 장관은 백악관 상황실에서 스콧 베센트 재무장관, 피트 헤그세스 전쟁부 장관, 제이미슨 그리어 무역대표부(USTR) 대표, 마코 루비오 국무장관 겸 국가안보보좌관과 회의를 가졌습니다. 이 자리에서 베센트 장관은 상무부가 왜 수출 통제, 특히 스파이 스캔들의 중심에 있는 '메가스피드(Megaspeed)'에 대한 조치를 미루고 있는지 러트닉 장관을 추궁했고, 참석자들은 베센트 장관 편에 섰습니다. 러트닉 장관은 동의하는 듯했지만 "대통령께 확인해 봐야 한다"고 중얼거렸고, 한 참석자가 "좋습니다. 그럼 오늘 바로 합시다"라고 맞받았습니다. 일행은 오후 5시쯤 대통령 집무실(오벌 오피스)로 향했습니다. 트럼프 대통령은 기술 자문인 일론 머스크에게 전화를 걸어 의견을 들었고, 머스크는 루비오·베센트·그리어·헤그세스 장관 쪽 손을 들어줬습니다. 러트닉 장관은 "중국과 무역전쟁을 일으킬 것"이라고 경고했지만, 다른 참석자들은 "중국은 이미 러트닉이 우려하는 일을 우리에게 하고 있다"고 반박했습니다. 결국 트럼프 대통령은 "해치우자"며 결단을 내렸습니다. 그러나 집무실을 나선 뒤 러트닉 장관은 "몇 가지 방안을 마련해 다시 보고하겠다"며 또다시 시간을 끌었고, 한 소식통은 "모두가 '아니다, 결정은 이미 내려졌으니 당장 실행하라'고 했다. 그런데 아직도 실행되지 않았다"고 전했습니다. 한 관계자는 "그가 시간을 끌며 무산시키고 있다"며, 러트닉 장관이 앞서 대통령을 따로 만나 생각을 바꾸게 한 적도 있다고 말했습니다. 트럼프 대통령은 지난 5월과 8월, 그리고 11월 5일 등 최소 세 차례 엔비디아 칩 중국 유출 의심 기업에 대한 조치를 승인했지만, 러트닉 장관과 제프리 케슬러 상무부 차관이 베센트 장관 등의 압박에도 버텨 왔다고 악시오스는 전했습니다. 특히 지난 5월에는 젠슨 황 엔비디아 CEO와 미 정보당국이 중국 요원으로 의심하는 메가스피드 직원 앨리스 황의 관계를 경고하는 극비 메모가 대통령과 고위 당국자들에게 공유됐고, 이후 회의에서 베센트 장관, 제이 클레이턴 국가정보국장, 헤그세스 장관과 백악관 관계자들이 조치를 촉구했지만 러트닉 장관과 케슬러 차관이 거부했다고 합니다. 상무부의 크리스틴 아이카머 대변인은 베센트 장관이 러트닉 장관을 추궁했다는 내용을 부인했으며, 다른 주장에 대해서는 즉각 답변하지 않았습니다. 트럼프 행정부는 지난해 25% 관세를 조건으로 구형이지만 여전히 강력한 엔비디아 H200 칩의 대중국 판매를 허용한 바 있습니다. 젠슨 황 CEO는 저성능 칩을 중국에 팔아야 중국의 자체 기술 개발을 막고 미국 의존도를 유지할 수 있다며 트럼프 대통령과 러트닉 장관을 설득해 왔습니다. 수출 통제 정책은 상무부 소관이지만, 최종 결정권자는 트럼프 대통령입니다.

items.original_title: FinancialJuice: Deutsche Bank's View on US CPI

evidence.headline: FinancialJuice: Deutsche Bank's View on US CPI
evidence.snippet: The CPI release got more attention than usual, partly because of comments from Fed Governor Waller a few hours beforehand. He was speaking in London, where he said that “if the October CPI inflation data out later today are similar to the past two monthly readings - with core CPI inflation around 0.3 percent or even higher”, then he thought “a 50 basis point hike in the policy rate should be considered at the December meeting”. Indeed, he also said that in those circumstances, a 25bp hike “would put our credibility at risk”. So when the core CPI print was confirmed at 0.3%, that led to mounting speculation about a larger rate hike. That impact was clear from market pricing, with the amount of hikes for a December up from 21.0bps on Monday to 27.7bps by last night’s close, and 28.5bps this morning. So in other words, a 25bp hike is fully priced in, with futures also pricing in a 14% chance of a larger 50bp move. But it wasn’t just December that was affected, with markets pricing in a more hawkish profile further out the curve as well. Indeed, the rate priced in for the September 2027 meeting was up +22.3bps yesterday, so investors had priced in almost a full additional rate hike to next year’s path. Meanwhile, DB’s own US economists have updated their Fed view, adding a rate hike in January to their profile. So they now expect three more 25bp hikes at the next three meetings (Dec, Jan and March).

items.original_title: FinancialJuice: Citi's Summary of JPY Weakness

evidence.headline: FinancialJuice: Citi's Summary of JPY Weakness
evidence.snippet: We think the weakness of the JPY in the first half of this year was due to JPY-sale hedging by overseas investors who invest in Japanese equities with a forex-neutral strategy. The market cap of the Japanese equity market has grown by around ¥400trn over the past year. One-third of this is held by overseas investors, and if we assume that 20% of their holdings are under a forex-neutral strategy then JPY- sale hedging will have increased by some¥24trn during this time. During this period the flow of equity investment into Japan from overseas was more than ¥20trn (Figure 1). If 80% of this was unhedged, then it would have resulted in JPY buying of around ¥16trn. This means the scale of JPY-sale hedging would have been almost ¥10trn greater than JPY buying due to new investment. In all markets, not just the forex market, selling must match buying. The exposure needing to be hedged increased rapidly due to gains by the equity market, so there was likely to be a very strong necessity to sell the JPY among investors adopting a forex-neutral strategy (Figure 2).

items.original_title: FinancialJuice: Goldman Sachs on Fed

evidence.headline: FinancialJuice: Goldman Sachs on Fed
evidence.snippet: We continue to expect a second 25bp rate hike in December and are adding a third 25bp hike to our forecast in March 2027. A third hike could come earlier in January, but we think March is a bit more likely because we expect the November and December inflation reports to be softer but then expect larger start-of-the-year price increases amidst ongoing cost pressures to boost inflation in January We remain confident that inflation will be meaningfully lower by the end of 2027 as the effects of tariffs, the energy shock, and AI price pressures diminish But we suspect that the recent inflation prints will lead most FOMC participants to signal a third hike in the December dot plot and that a firmer January inflation report would make delivering it the path of least resistance even if the energy shock appears over by then We have left our forecast for the eventual terminal fed funds rate unchanged at 3.25-3.5%, but we now expect rate cuts to begin one quarter later in December 2027 (vs. September 2027 previously), followed by additional cuts in March, June, and September 2028.

items.original_title: FinancialJuice: UniCredit: AI Debt and Bonds

evidence.headline: FinancialJuice: UniCredit: AI Debt and Bonds
evidence.snippet: The five major hyperscalers plan to invest USD 4-6tn in data centres in 2025-30. As a large part of the funding will come from public and private debt markets, this historically unprecedented capex cycle creates a number of credit-relevant ramifications, including for European markets. Hyperscalers are increasingly tapping foreign debt markets, having issued EUR 52bn of euro-denominated reverse Yankees in 2025 and 2026 to date. This corresponds to around 25% of total euro-denominated reverse Yankees placed during that time. We see scope for up to an additional EUR 5-10bn this year. So far, this issuance has had an adverse impact on the relative performance of the technology sector, although its impact on government bonds has been contained, given the limited issuance relative to outstanding government debt and hyperscalers’ avoidance of maturities heavily used by governments. Roughly 40% of total investment will be funded via the bond market. While increased bond issuance will expand the technology sector’s weight and duration in credit markets, the greater concern is the risk of excessive investment, deterioration of credit quality and defaults. Moreover, rapid technological progress and improvements in AI model efficiency could reduce future infrastructure needs, making long-term demand difficult to forecast. Separately, the outcome of the US midterm elections increases the likelihood of greater regulation of hyperscalers, potentially creating additional challenges for competitive dynamics, financing structures and asset valuations.

evidence.headline: FinancialJuice: Credit Ágricole: US CPI
evidence.snippet: Looking at the details, it is hard to place the blame on volatile components this month, as could be done (at least in part) over the past couple of months when we had seen some noise involved in the strength. Thus, we see the October report as a genuinely firm one. Core goods did come in a bit below our expectations at 0.16% MoM SA vs our take of 0.25% MoM SA, though this was in large part due to weaker used cars, so possible noise on the downside in this case. Services, by contrast, came in higher than expected at 0.34% MoM SA vs our take of 0.25% MoM SA, with a much more limited contribution from volatile components than the past couple of months. Looking ahead, we will of course fine-tune our forecasts as usual, but for now we see headline remaining below what we expect to represent a peak in May, hovering in the mid-3% YoY range through Q127, with core in a relatively narrow 2.7-2.9% YoY band through Q127 before seeing some modest improvement later in 2027. For the Fed, we had previously argued that consecutive hikes would have been a better approach than an every-other-meeting pace, and today’s data raises the question as to why the Fed did not just hike in October. Given that it did not, however, the upside surprise in October CPI on top of the firm September report should basically lock in a hike at the December meeting, where we maintain our base case of a 25bp hike. Governor Christopher Waller’s comments earlier this morning would even raise the possibility of a 50bp move, though we are not quite sure today’s data will reach the bar for a jumbo hike from the broader Committee.
